paragraphs.text: Hospitals are rethinking the design of their wards. Architect Laura Stein argues that single rooms should replace large shared wards, because patients sleep better and infections spread less easily when each person has their own space.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Nurse manager Paul Okoro is not convinced. He points out that nurses can see many patients at once on an open ward, and that in single rooms, patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A study by the National Health Research Institute compared both designs in six hospitals. It found fewer infections in single rooms but no difference in how long patients stayed, and it concluded that the higher building costs were justified only for certain patients.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Patient groups add another view. The Patients’ Voice charity reports that older patients often feel lonely in single rooms and would prefer small shared bays of four beds, a design that Stein says she is willing to include.
paragraphs.label: D
